newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Relief in sight for NZ exporters - ANZ Bank.
newsitem.headline: Relief in sight for NZ exporters - ANZ Bank.

text.p: The struggling export sector should benefit from lower short-term interest rates, the New Zealand Press Association on Monday reported ANZ Bank as saying.
ANZ chief economist Paul Stewart said falling interest rates in the short term should relieve upward pressure on New Zealand's strong dollar and help the country's exporters.

The drop in price competitiveness incurred by exports from New Zealand's rising dollar would not be fully restored, but a more stable exchange rate, combined with improvements in the global economy, should provide relief to the New Zealand export sector, he said.
While much attention had centred on the exchange rate, a slow-down in the global economy had contributed to a significant dampening effect on export conditions.

"Not all exporters are under pressure. And for those that are, not all the blame can be put on the dollar. For example, industrial production growth of the world's developed countries has fallen from 6 percent in 1993-1994 to about 1 percent in 1996.
"New Zealand is not the only economy experiencing a slowdown. (International) export markets for agriculture and manufacturing have been subdued," Stewart said.

ANZ believes with falling inflation and the Reserve Bank's inflation target being extended to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent following the coalition government deal last Tuesday, the central bank is likely to accept lower interest rates.

Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash will announce his view on the economy on Tuesday, in the RBNZ's six monthly monetary policy statement. Commentators expect Brash to be comfortable with recent falls in interest rates.
